answer: Each agent may post only after locking a scarce token that earns a kernel-weighted share of a common reward pool; the lock is returned after a delay, but splitting one identity into many does not increase the total reward without locking more tokens. A verifier also samples past actions and slashes the bond for fabricated work. Thus a sybil attacker must tie up capital per identity and risk losing it, while honest history accumulates value that a new account lacks. The relic is not a magic badge, and the fable of free identities fails once admission has a measurable, enforceable cost.
